existing_interactions.hypothesis: Red-zone play-calling x team total: when a high team total comes from field goals and explosive plays rather than goal-line passing, QB TD counts are lower than the total suggests.
Pressure x turnover-worthy throws: pressure raises INT probability mostly for QBs with high aggressiveness, while a zone defense with ball skills converts more of the bad throws.
Trailing script x INT rate: increased attempts and deeper throws when trailing push INT counts up, interplaying with game spread and opponent pass rush.
TD luck x QB rushing: QBs with goal-line rushing use convert fewer passing TDs even with high red-zone volume.

qb_passing_tds_and_ints.existing_mechanism: Passing TDs = red-zone and goal-line pass trips x conversion; team scoring expectation and the run/pass split near the goal line determine opportunities, and passing TD luck regresses strongly. Interceptions = attempts x INT rate, where INT rate mixes QB turnover-worthy throw rate, pressure, aggressiveness, throw depth and defender luck. Both are low-count Poisson-like events whose means depend on script, opponent pass rush/ball skills, weather and QB health.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Pressure rate x time to throw: pressure harms a slow-release QB far more than a quick-release one, so expected efficiency loss from a strong pass rush must be scaled by individual time to throw and screen/quick-game usage.
Spread x pass rate: a double-digit underdog's QB gains attempts but meets defenses in prevent shells; yardage rises less than attempts, and the favorite's QB loses garbage-time volume.
Wind x deep passing: wind above ~15 mph removes air yards for high-aDOT offenses while quick-game QBs are less affected; the effect on the yardage mean is larger than on attempts.
Coverage shell x target distribution: against heavy two-high zone, TE/RB targets and short completions rise and deep yards fall, so a QB's yards depend on whether his receivers win underneath.
Receiver availability x pressure: loss of the top WR plus a pressured pocket lowers both separation and time, compounding efficiency loss.

qb_passing_yards.existing_mechanism: Passing yards = dropbacks x (1 - sack rate) x attempt share x completion rate x yards per completion. Volume comes from expected plays (pace), neutral pass rate (PROE) and game script from the spread; efficiency from opponent-adjusted EPA per dropback, air yards and CPOE, and is modified by pressure faced (OL versus pass rush, time to throw), coverage shell and target distribution, receiver and OL availability, weather and roof. The distribution is right-skewed, with garbage-time and overtime volume in the tail and injury exit in the left tail.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Spread x run rate: a heavy favorite leading late converts to many carries, but the carries go to whichever back is on the field (often the backup), so the starter's carry share is score-state-dependent.
